## `boatramp`

boatramp — self-hosted, streaming-first static site publishing (server + CLI in one binary)

**Usage:** `boatramp [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>`

These global options are accepted on **every** subcommand (listed once here, omitted from the per-command tables below):

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--config <CONFIG>` | — | — | — | Path to the config file. Defaults to `project.cfg` for the project commands and `boatramp.cfg` for `serve` |
| `--project <PROJECT>` | `BOATRAMP_PROJECT` | — | — | Target project for site-scoped commands (default `default`; falls back to `[publish].project`; env `BOATRAMP_PROJECT`) |
| `--output-format <OUTPUT_FORMAT>` | `BOATRAMP_OUTPUT_FORMAT` | `human` | human \| json | How to render command results: `human` (default) or `json`. Applies to every subcommand |

Run the HTTP server and publishing API

(On a cluster node it still opts the node-local Raft store into the tail repair — the cluster stays strict.) |
| `--strict-kv` | `BOATRAMP_KV_STRICT` | — | — | Restore the pre-v0.9.0 FAIL-LOUD-on-any-torn-store behavior for the single-node control-plane SlateDB store (paranoid mode): a torn tail is NOT auto-quarantined — the node fails loud naming `kv recover` and (via C5) binds a recovery-mode listener rather than serving. | `--dns-publish-provider <DNS_PUBLISH_PROVIDER>` | `BOATRAMP_DNS_PUBLISH_PROVIDER` | — | — | DNS provider backing the guest **`dns-publish` WRITE** capability (cap-req #24/#25) — which host-held credential performs a granted guest's DNS mutations. Mirrors `--acme-dns-provider` (`manual` \| `cloudflare` \| `route53` \| `oci` \| …); **credentials come from the ENVIRONMENT** (the same per-provider vars `boatramp dns --help` documents), NEVER the config file. **UNSET (the default) ⇒ no provider is wired ⇒ every guest `dns-publish` call fail-closes to `access-denied`** — unchanged for an operator who does not opt in. `manual` installs the credential-free Manual provider (records/echoes the intended writes) for an offline proof. The node posture `allow_guest_dns_publish` (off by default) + a per-handler `dns_publish_zones` allowlist still gate every write. Flag/env > `[serve.dns_publish].provider`. (DISTINCT from `--acme-dns-provider`, which is the ACME cert-issuance DNS credential, a separate authority.) |

| `--acme-wildcard-preview` | `BOATRAMP_ACME_WILDCARD_PREVIEW` | `false` | — | With `--tls acme-dns`, also issue a `*.deploy.<domain>` wildcard cert so the wildcard preview host form gets TLS |
| `--acme-propagation-wait-secs <ACME_PROPAGATION_WAIT_SECS>` | `BOATRAMP_ACME_PROPAGATION_WAIT` | `45` | — | DNS-01 only: **maximum** seconds to wait for the `_acme-challenge` TXT to become visible in the zone before telling the CA to validate. This is a real readiness poll (resolve the record and confirm the expected value), not a blind sleep — issuance proceeds the moment the record is live, and only falls back to proceeding-anyway (the CA retries) if this elapses first |
| `--acme-propagation-poll-interval-secs <ACME_PROPAGATION_POLL_INTERVAL_SECS>` | `BOATRAMP_ACME_PROPAGATION_POLL_INTERVAL` | `2` | — | DNS-01 only: how often (seconds) to re-check DNS while waiting for the `_acme-challenge` TXT to propagate |
| `--dns-target <DNS_TARGET>` | `BOATRAMP_DNS_TARGET` | — | — | `--tls acme-dns` only: point every site's **verified custom domains** (`domain add`/`domain verify`-attached hosts; never the `*.deploy.<host>` preview wildcard, which is managed by the ACME-DNS setup above) at this address, kept converged by a leader-gated background reconcile (capability #24 Stage 6). An IPv4/IPv6 literal becomes an A/AAAA record; anything else a CNAME (e.g. a load balancer hostname) — the same convention as `dns configure-domain --target`. Unset (the default) disables the loop entirely; `dns configure-domain` remains the manual, one-shot path |
| `--dns-reconcile-tick-secs <DNS_RECONCILE_TICK_SECS>` | `BOATRAMP_DNS_RECONCILE_TICK` | `300` | — | How often the `--dns-target` reconcile loop re-sweeps every site's verified custom domains (seconds). Ignored when `--dns-target` is unset |
| `--dns-reconcile-ttl <DNS_RECONCILE_TTL>` | `BOATRAMP_DNS_RECONCILE_TTL` | `300` | — | TTL (seconds) for the A/AAAA/CNAME records the `--dns-target` reconcile loop writes. Ignored when `--dns-target` is unset |
| `--max-upload-bytes <MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES>` | `BOATRAMP_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` | — | — | Reject blob uploads larger than this many bytes (default: unlimited). Flag/env > `serve.max_upload_bytes` |
| `--upload-idle-timeout-secs <UPLOAD_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECS>` | `BOATRAMP_UPLOAD_IDLE_TIMEOUT` | — | — | Abort an upload whose body stalls (no bytes received) for longer than this many seconds — slowloris protection. Flag/env > `serve.upload_idle_timeout_secs` |
| `--max-concurrent-uploads <MAX_CONCURRENT_UPLOADS>` | `BOATRAMP_MAX_CONCURRENT_UPLOADS` | — | — | Cap simultaneous blob uploads; further uploads get 503 until a slot frees. Flag/env > `serve.max_concurrent_uploads` |
| `--http-redirect-addr <HTTP_REDIRECT_ADDR>` | `BOATRAMP_HTTP_REDIRECT_ADDR` | — | — | In a TLS mode, also bind this plain-HTTP address (e.g. `0.0.0.0:80`) on a second listener that 308-redirects every request to HTTPS. Flag/env > `serve.http_redirect_addr`. Ignored when `--tls off` |
| `--default-site <DEFAULT_SITE>` | `BOATRAMP_DEFAULT_SITE` | — | — | Site to serve for a `Host` that matches no domain, instead of 404 (catch-all). Flag/env > `serve.default_site` |
| `--pop-origin <POP_ORIGIN>` | `BOATRAMP_POP_ORIGIN` | — | — | The fleet's canonical public origin (e.g. `https://cp.example.com`) that a per-request proof-of-possession must bind to. Required for holder-bound (`cnf`/PoP) tokens; compared against a proof's origin, never a request header. Flag/env > `serve.pop_origin` |
| `--cluster-rate-limit` | `BOATRAMP_CLUSTER_RATE_LIMIT` | — | — | Rate-limit cluster-wide via the control-plane KV (shared fixed-window) instead of per-node in-process buckets. Meaningful with a shared/ replicated KV; adds a KV round-trip per limited request. Flag/env > `serve.cluster_rate_limit` |
| `--cluster-init` | `BOATRAMP_CLUSTER_INIT` | — | — | **Found a brand-new cluster** from this node (the explicit, one-time genesis signal — F5). Required to bring up the first node with no seeds; refused if `[cluster].seeds` are set (a node either founds or joins, not both). A no-op once the node has durable state (restart resumes) |
| `--cluster-advertise-addr <CLUSTER_ADVERTISE_ADDR>` | `BOATRAMP_CLUSTER_ADVERTISE_ADDR` | — | — | This node's own mesh base URL that peers should dial to reach it (e.g. `https://10.0.0.4:7000`). | `--cluster-join <CLUSTER_JOIN>` | `BOATRAMP_CLUSTER_JOIN` | — | — | **Join an existing cluster** using a one-paste ticket from `cluster add` (bundles the seeds + root anchor + single-use token). Overrides `[cluster].seeds`/`root_pubkeys`/`join_token`. Mutually exclusive with `--cluster-init` |
| `--shared-cache-coherence` | `BOATRAMP_SHARED_CACHE_COHERENCE` | — | — | Keep the local config cache coherent across processes sharing one KV (Cloudflare KV / shared SlateDB): publish each control-plane write to a changelog and poll it to invalidate just the keys peers changed. Turn on when running multiple stateless frontends over one shared store; unnecessary single-node or in a Raft cluster. Flag/env > `serve.shared_cache_coherence` |
| `--protect-previews` | `BOATRAMP_PROTECT_PREVIEWS` | — | — | Require a valid control-plane token to view deployment previews (`/_deploy/<id>` and `<id>.deploy.<host>`). Flag/env > `serve.protect_previews` |
| `--http3` | — | — | — | Also serve HTTP/3 (QUIC) on the same UDP port (with `--tls custom`). Requires the `http3` build feature |
| `--oidc-issuer <OIDC_ISSUER>` | `BOATRAMP_OIDC_ISSUER` | — | — | OIDC issuer URL for control-plane bearer-JWT auth (its JWKS is fetched at startup; tokens' scope claim must carry boatramp scopes). Requires the `oidc` build feature |

## `boatramp forward`

Forward a local port to an in-cluster target over the overlay fabric — relay-blind, capability-gated, `ssh -L`-shaped (requires `--features overlay`)

**Usage:** `boatramp forward [OPTIONS] <LOCAL> [TARGET]`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<LOCAL>` | — | — | — | Local address to bind and forward (e.g. `127.0.0.1:5432`) |
| `[TARGET]` | — | — | — | The in-cluster service to reach (e.g. `svc/db`). Resolved via the control plane when no `--ticket`/explicit flags are given. Optional with `--ticket` (the ticket's service wins); if both are given they must match |
| `--ticket <TICKET>` | — | — | — | A forward ticket (`brfwd1.…`) from `boatramp overlay grant` — a control-plane-less path |
| `--server <SERVER>` | `BOATRAMP_SERVER` | — | — | boatramp server base URL for self-serve resolution (overrides `[publish].server`) |
| `--relay <RELAY>` | — | — | — | The cluster relay/ingress socket address to dial (explicit escape hatch) |
| `--relay-id <RELAY_ID>` | — | — | — | The relay's overlay identity to pin (`bro1…` or `ed25519:<hex>`) |
| `--egress-id <EGRESS_ID>` | — | — | — | The egress/terminator's overlay identity to pin for the E2EE session |
| `--token <TOKEN>` | — | — | — | The dial capability token (COSE), holder-bound to this client's identity |
| `--token-file <TOKEN_FILE>` | — | — | — | Read the dial token from a file instead of `--token` |
| `--identity <IDENTITY>` | — | — | — | This client's overlay identity seed — `ed25519:<hex>` inline, or a path to a file holding it. Optional with a convenience `--ticket` (which carries the identity); required otherwise and with a `--holder-pub` ticket |
| `--capability-only` | — | — | — | Dial the relay server-auth-only (present NO client certificate) — for a **capability-only** relay reached via `--ticket`/explicit flags (where the egress is the authority). Self-serve learns the relay's posture from the control plane and sets this automatically |

## `boatramp expose`

Publish a LOCAL service INTO the cluster overlay (the reverse of `forward`) — the exposer dials the relay outbound and holds it open, so a cluster-side `boatramp forward svc/<name>` reaches a NAT'd local service, relay-blind and capability-gated (requires `--features overlay`)

**Usage:** `boatramp expose [OPTIONS] <LOCAL> [SERVICE]`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<LOCAL>` | — | — | — | The LOCAL service address to publish (e.g. `127.0.0.1:5432`) — what the exposer connects to for each inbound flow |
| `[SERVICE]` | — | — | — | The in-cluster service name to publish AS (e.g. `svc/db`), optionally preceded by the literal `as`. Optional with `--ticket` (the ticket's service wins); if both are given they must match |
| `--ticket <TICKET>` | — | — | — | An expose ticket (`brexp1.…`) from `boatramp overlay grant-expose` — the one-flag path |
| `--relay <RELAY>` | — | — | — | The cluster relay/ingress socket address to dial OUT to (explicit escape hatch) |
| `--relay-id <RELAY_ID>` | — | — | — | The relay's overlay identity to pin (`bro1…` or `ed25519:<hex>`) |
| `--token <TOKEN>` | — | — | — | The overlay-publish capability token (COSE), holder-bound to this exposer's identity |
| `--token-file <TOKEN_FILE>` | — | — | — | Read the publish token from a file instead of `--token` |
| `--trust-root <TRUST_ROOT>` | — | — | — | The cluster trust root's PUBLIC key (`ed25519:`/`es256:` tagged hex) — the exposer verifies each incoming forward client's dial capability against it (zero-trust terminator). Carried by a `--ticket`; required with the explicit flags |
| `--identity <IDENTITY>` | — | — | — | This exposer's overlay identity seed — `ed25519:<hex>` inline, or a path to a file holding it. Optional with a convenience `--ticket` (which carries the identity); required otherwise and with a `--holder-pub` ticket. Its public half MUST equal the publish capability's holder |
| `--capability-only` | — | — | — | Dial the relay server-auth-only (present NO client certificate) — for a **capability-only** relay, where the registration's E2EE handshake (not a TLS pin) proves the exposer's identity. The common expose case (a NAT'd exposer needs no pre-enrollment). Omit for a mutual-pin relay (the exposer presents its cert and must be in the relay's `allowed_clients`). Ignored on self-serve (the posture is taken from the control plane) |
| `--server <SERVER>` | `BOATRAMP_SERVER` | — | — | boatramp server base URL for self-serve resolution (overrides `[publish].server`). With neither `--ticket` nor `--relay`, `boatramp expose <local> as svc/<name>` resolves the relay topology + mints the publish capability over the control plane (`POST /api/overlay/expose`, `Overlay·Admin`), authenticated by your boatramp token — zero hand-typed topology |

## `boatramp overlay`

Admin tooling for the overlay forward-flow: mint a dial capability and emit a one-flag forward ticket (`overlay grant`) for `boatramp forward --ticket` (requires `--features overlay`)

**Usage:** `boatramp overlay <COMMAND>`

### `boatramp overlay grant`

Mint a dial capability for `service` and emit a one-flag forward ticket

**Usage:** `boatramp overlay grant [OPTIONS] <SERVICE>`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<SERVICE>` | — | — | — | The in-cluster service to authorize (e.g. `svc/db`); must match the relay's route and the egress's service name |
| `--relay <RELAY>` | — | — | — | The relay/ingress socket address the client will dial (`host:port`) |
| `--relay-id <RELAY_ID>` | — | — | — | The relay's overlay identity to pin (`ed25519:<hex>` or `bro1…`) |
| `--egress-id <EGRESS_ID>` | — | — | — | The egress/terminator's overlay identity to pin for the E2EE session |
| `--holder-pub <HOLDER_PUB>` | — | — | — | Bind the capability to a client identity the client already generated (its public `ed25519:<hex>`/`bro1…`); the ticket then carries no secret and the client supplies `--identity`. Omit to have the grant generate the client identity and embed its seed in the ticket (convenience — the ticket is then secret) |
| `--ttl-secs <TTL_SECS>` | — | `3600` | — | Capability lifetime in seconds (an overlay-dial capability must be time-bounded) |
| `--config <CONFIG>` | — | `boatramp.cfg` | — | Path to the config holding the root signer (`[serve.signer]` / `auth_root_private_key`) |

### `boatramp overlay grant-expose`

Mint an overlay-publish capability for `service` and emit a one-flag EXPOSE ticket for `boatramp expose --ticket` (the reverse-ingress analog of `grant`)

**Usage:** `boatramp overlay grant-expose [OPTIONS] <SERVICE>`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<SERVICE>` | — | — | — | The in-cluster service to publish AS (e.g. `svc/db`); must match the relay's registry key and the exposer's `expose <local> as svc/<name>` |
| `--relay <RELAY>` | — | — | — | The relay/ingress socket address the exposer will dial OUT to (`host:port`) |
| `--relay-id <RELAY_ID>` | — | — | — | The relay's overlay identity to pin (`ed25519:<hex>` or `bro1…`) |
| `--holder-pub <HOLDER_PUB>` | — | — | — | Bind the capability to an exposer identity it already generated (its public `ed25519:<hex>`/`bro1…`); the ticket then carries no secret and the exposer supplies `--identity`. Omit to have the grant generate the exposer identity and embed its seed |
| `--ttl-secs <TTL_SECS>` | — | `3600` | — | Capability lifetime in seconds (an overlay-publish capability must be time-bounded) |
| `--config <CONFIG>` | — | `boatramp.cfg` | — | Path to the config holding the root signer (`[serve.signer]` / `auth_root_private_key`) |

### `boatramp overlay invite`

Mint a single-use overlay-ENROLL invitation for a role + scope and emit a one-flag `brojoin1.…` enrollment ticket for `boatramp overlay join`

**Usage:** `boatramp overlay invite [OPTIONS]`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--role <ROLE>` | — | — | node \| device \| workload | The role the invitation grants once redeemed |
| `--scope <SCOPE>` | — | — | — | The service scope the enrollee may dial/expose once enrolled (e.g. `svc/db`, or `*`) |
| `--ttl-secs <TTL_SECS>` | — | `3600` | — | Invitation lifetime in seconds (an enrollment invitation MUST be time-bounded) |
| `--relay <RELAY>` | — | — | — | The relay's overlay identity to pin once enrolled (`ed25519:<hex>`/`bro1…`); advisory, carried in the ticket for the enrollee's reference |
| `--config <CONFIG>` | — | `boatramp.cfg` | — | Path to the config holding the root signer (`[serve.signer]` / `auth_root_private_key`) |

### `boatramp overlay join`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<TOKEN>` | — | — | — | The `brojoin1.…` enrollment ticket from `boatramp overlay invite` |
| `--identity <IDENTITY>` | — | — | — | The overlay identity to enroll: a tagged seed (`ed25519:<hex>`) or a path to a key file. Omit to load-or-generate this operator's persistent identity (as `overlay id` does) |
| `--server <SERVER>` | `BOATRAMP_SERVER` | — | — | boatramp server base URL to redeem against (overrides `[publish].server`) |

Print this operator's overlay identity (load-or-generate at `~/.config/boatramp/overlay.key`). This is the identity self-serve `boatramp forward svc/<name>` binds its dial capability to

**Usage:** `boatramp overlay id`

Resolve one overlay service name to its topology (relay + egress identities)

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<NAME>` | — | — | — | The service name (e.g. `svc/db`) |
| `--server <SERVER>` | `BOATRAMP_SERVER` | — | — | boatramp server base URL (overrides `[publish].server`) |

### `boatramp overlay pair`

Pair with another operator's device and mutually verify identities with a short authentication string (SAS), detecting an active man-in-the-middle

**Usage:** `boatramp overlay pair [OPTIONS] [PEER_OR_CODE]`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `[PEER_OR_CODE]` | — | — | — | Act as the INITIATOR: either a peer `host:port` to DIRECT-DIAL (the address the responder is listening on), or a `bropair1…` rendezvous code to REDEEM through the cluster relay |
| `--listen <ADDR>` | — | — | — | Act as the DIRECT-DIAL RESPONDER: listen on this `host:port` for a pairing dialer |
| `--accept <CODE>` | — | — | — | Act as the RELAY-RENDEZVOUS RESPONDER: park this `bropair1…` code at the cluster relay and wait for the NAT'd peer to redeem it (for peers that cannot direct-dial). Mint a code with `overlay pair-code` |
| `--park-cap <CAP>` | — | — | — | Only meaningful with `--accept`: present this holder-bound `overlay-pairing-park` capability (from `overlay pair-code --accepter-pubkey`, the `park_cap` it prints) and prove possession of it to the relay — REQUIRED when the relay's `pairing_park` config is `"authenticated"`; omit for an OPEN-mode relay (today's default), where it is never sent |
| `--short <CODE>` | — | — | — | Act as the INITIATOR over the human-typeable SHORT-CODE path: redeem this short code (e.g. `1234-5678`; separators optional) via the control plane's unauthenticated relay-topology lookup (`GET /api/overlay/pair-relay` — a short code carries no topology of its own), then the relay's rate-limited short-redeem. Mint one with `overlay pair-code --short` |
| `--identity <IDENTITY>` | — | — | — | The overlay identity to pair AS: a tagged seed (`ed25519:<hex>`) or a key-file path. Omit to use this operator's persistent identity (as `overlay id`) |
| `--expect <SAS_WORDS>` | — | — | — | Non-interactive confirm: the FULL expected SAS words (e.g. `cargo-delta-hotel`), as shown on the PEER's device, compared case-insensitively. The pairing ABORTS unless the derived SAS equals this — there is no check-skipping `--yes`. Required when stdin is not a TTY |
| `--timeout-secs <TIMEOUT_SECS>` | — | `30` | — | Bound the pairing window in seconds (the handshake must complete within it; the wait for a peer to redeem a parked rendezvous is bounded separately by the relay's rendezvous TTL) |
| `--server <SERVER>` | `BOATRAMP_SERVER` | — | — | boatramp server base URL (overrides `[publish].server`) — used ONLY by the `--short` path, to look up the relay topology (`GET /api/overlay/pair-relay`); every other transport needs no control-plane call |

### `boatramp overlay pair-code`

Mint a single-use, short-TTL PAIRING rendezvous code (`bropair1…`) so two peers that cannot direct-dial each other (both NAT'd) can meet through the cluster relay, which bridges their ciphertext blind. Gated `Overlay·Admin` at the server (`POST /api/overlay/pair-code`). Share the printed code with the new peer: park it with `overlay pair --accept <code>`, and the peer redeems it with `overlay pair <code>`

**Usage:** `boatramp overlay pair-code [OPTIONS]`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--ttl-secs <TTL_SECS>` | — | `300` | — | Code lifetime in seconds (a pairing code is short-lived — minutes; the server clamps it) |
| `--short` | — | — | — | ALSO mint a human-typeable pairing SHORT CODE (e.g. `1234-5678`) aliasing the same rendezvous — easier to read aloud / type on a second device than `bropair1…`. Low-entropy by design; the relay rate-limits + locks out online guessing on redeem |
| `--accepter-pubkey <PUBKEY>` | — | — | — | The ACCEPTER's overlay public key (`ed25519:<hex>`/`bro1…`, e.g. from their `overlay id`) — REQUIRED when this cluster's relay runs AUTHENTICATED pairing-park (`[overlay] pairing_park = "authenticated"`), in which case the mint ALSO returns a holder-bound `overlay-pairing-park` capability bound to this key: give that capability to the accepter alongside the code (they present it with `overlay pair --accept <code> --park-cap <cap>`). Ignored (and optional) against an OPEN-mode relay (today's default) |
| `--server <SERVER>` | `BOATRAMP_SERVER` | — | — | boatramp server base URL (overrides `[publish].server`) |

### `boatramp overlay policy`

Manage the cluster's **overlay flow policy** — the per-flow access gate that decides which dial/publish-cap mints the control plane will issue (deny-or-shrink-TTL only), separate from the RBAC that grants `Overlay·Write`/`Admin`. All three verbs are `System·Admin`

**Usage:** `boatramp overlay policy <COMMAND>`

#### `boatramp overlay policy ls`

Show the active overlay flow policy (Cedar text) + its version (`GET /api/overlay/policy`)

**Usage:** `boatramp overlay policy ls [OPTIONS]`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--server <SERVER>` | `BOATRAMP_SERVER` | — | — | boatramp server base URL (overrides `[publish].server`) |

#### `boatramp overlay policy set`

Replace the overlay flow policy from a `.cedar` file (or `-` for stdin) (`PUT /api/overlay/policy`). Validated server-side (parse + schema + temporal screen); a validation failure prints the server's `400` body verbatim. An EMPTY file turns the gate OFF. Storing the FIRST policy surfaces a default-deny CLIFF warning

**Usage:** `boatramp overlay policy set [OPTIONS] <FILE>`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<FILE>` | — | — | — | Path to the `.cedar` policy file, or `-` to read the policy from stdin |
| `--if-match <IF_MATCH>` | — | — | — | Expected current version (the `version` from `policy ls`) for a conditional write; a stale version → `409` (re-read + retry). Omit to overwrite the current value |
| `--server <SERVER>` | `BOATRAMP_SERVER` | — | — | boatramp server base URL (overrides `[publish].server`) |

#### `boatramp overlay policy test`

Dry-run a dial/expose mint against the active (or a supplied) policy — NO capability is minted (`POST /api/overlay/policy/test`). Prints ALLOW/DENY, the TTL ceiling, and the deciding policies + diagnostics (a `System·Admin`-only authoring aid)

**Usage:** `boatramp overlay policy test [OPTIONS]`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--action <ACTION>` | — | — | dial \| expose | The flow action to simulate |
| `--service <SERVICE>` | — | — | — | The target service name (e.g. `svc/db`) |
| `--holder <HOLDER>` | — | — | — | The holder key (`ed25519:<hex>` / `bro1…`); defaults to this operator's overlay id |
| `--role <ROLE>` | — | — | — | Simulate a bound member credential's role (`node`/`device`/`workload`); absent ⇒ key-only |
| `--scope <SCOPE>` | — | — | — | Simulate a bound member credential's service scope; absent ⇒ key-only |
| `--enrolled` | — | — | — | Simulate `enrolled = true` on the holder (a bound member credential was presented) |
| `--ttl-secs <TTL_SECS>` | — | `3600` | — | The requested TTL (seconds) to evaluate — the policy may shrink it |
| `--server <SERVER>` | `BOATRAMP_SERVER` | — | — | boatramp server base URL (overrides `[publish].server`) |

## `boatramp tunnel`

Reach overlay services BY NAME: a SOCKS5 (+ optional HTTP CONNECT) proxy daemon over the shared tunnel core (overlay-service-tunneler plan R1; requires `--features overlay`)

**Usage:** `boatramp tunnel [OPTIONS]`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--server <SERVER>` | `BOATRAMP_SERVER` | — | — | boatramp server base URL (overrides `[publish].server`) |
| `--socks <SOCKS>` | — | `127.0.0.1:1080` | — | Start the SOCKS5 front-end, bound to this address (plan §2). On by default — SOCKS is the only consumption front-end this release ships |
| `--http-connect <HTTP_CONNECT>` | — | — | — | Also start a small HTTP `CONNECT` front-end (for `HTTPS_PROXY`/`http.proxy`-style clients), bound to this address — reuses exactly the same dispatch and safety invariants as SOCKS |
| `--no-local-auth` | — | — | — | Disable the auto-generated local SOCKS credential (plan §5/§9.2 default is ON — a loopback port with no local auth lets ANY local user proxy under your overlay identity). Pass this only on a single-user host where that is an acceptable tradeoff |
| `--tun` | — | — | — | Start the TUN virtual-interface front-end instead of SOCKS (plan §3; Linux, macOS, and Windows). Needs the crate's `tun` cargo feature, plus privilege to open the device: `CAP_NET_ADMIN`/root on Linux, root on macOS, and Administrator (with the bundled `wintun.dll` alongside the binary) on Windows |
| `--cidr <CIDR>` | — | `100.64.0.0/10` | — | The synthetic CIDR routed into the TUN device (plan §3.2). Only meaningful with `--tun` |
| `--dns-zone <DNS_ZONE>` | — | `internal` | — | The embedded DNS zone's TLD (plan §3.3/§9 open decision 1 — operator-configurable, default `internal`, RFC 8375). Only meaningful with `--tun` |
| `--cluster <CLUSTER>` | — | — | — | The embedded DNS zone's `<cluster>` label (plan §3.3). Defaults to `[publish].project` from the project config, falling back to `default` if that is unset too. Only meaningful with `--tun` |
| `--cleanup` | — | — | — | Detect and revert a dirty-state marker left by a crashed previous `--tun` run (plan §3.9), then exit — does not start any front-end. Safe to run even with no marker present |
| `--max-connections <MAX_CONNECTIONS>` | — | `256` | — | Cap on concurrent accepted connections, SOCKS + HTTP CONNECT combined (Security MEDIUM-3 — bounds a local attacker opening connections faster than they're served) |
| `--allow-non-loopback` | — | — | — | Acknowledge binding `--socks`/`--http-connect` to a NON-loopback address (Security LOW-2). Absent this flag, a non-loopback bind is refused outright: this proxy resolves overlay services by name and dials under YOUR operator identity, so a LAN/0.0.0.0-exposed bind (especially combined with `--no-local-auth`) would hand anyone who can reach it an unauthenticated by-name proxy into your overlay |

## `boatramp domain`

Attach/detach hostnames to a site (virtualhost routing)

**Usage:** `boatramp domain [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--server <SERVER>` | `BOATRAMP_SERVER` | — | — | boatramp server base URL (overrides [deploy].server) |
| `--site <SITE>` | `BOATRAMP_SITE` | — | — | Site to edit (overrides [deploy].site) |

### `boatramp domain add`

Verify ownership of a hostname and attach it to the site (use `*.example.com` for a wildcard)

**Usage:** `boatramp domain add [OPTIONS] <HOST>`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<HOST>` | — | — | — | Hostname or `*.`-prefixed wildcard |
| `--method <METHOD>` | — | `http` | — | Verification method: `http` (default) serves a token file; `dns` publishes a TXT record (needs a server built with `domain-verify-dns`) |
| `--provider <PROVIDER>` | — | — | — | Managed-DNS provider (e.g. `cloudflare`, `digitalocean`, `route53`). When set, boatramp publishes the `_boatramp-verify` TXT for you (credentials from the environment; needs a build with `acme-dns`), waits for it to resolve, and attaches — no manual DNS edit. Implies `--method dns` and writes only the `_boatramp-verify` TXT, never the host's A/CNAME (that stays an explicit, post-verify step) |
| `--no-wait` | — | — | — | Only start the challenge and print instructions — skip the immediate verify+attach. Use when the host doesn't resolve here yet |
| `--unverified` | — | — | — | **Admin only.** Attach the host WITHOUT proving ownership — you assert it out-of-band. The host then serves normally (it bypasses the mandatory-verification gate). The server refuses this for a site-scoped token; it needs a `system·admin` token |

### `boatramp domain verify`

Check a hostname's verification challenge; on success it is attached

**Usage:** `boatramp domain verify <HOST>`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<HOST>` | — | — | — | Hostname or `*.`-prefixed wildcard |

### `boatramp domain rm`

Detach a hostname and drop its verification

**Usage:** `boatramp domain rm <HOST>`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<HOST>` | — | — | — | Hostname to remove |

### `boatramp domain ls`

List the site's hostnames and any pending verifications

**Usage:** `boatramp domain ls`

### `boatramp domain verify-records`

**Operator only.** Verify a set of DNS records resolve as expected (a read-only diagnostic — it attaches and persists nothing). Each `--record` is `KIND[/MODE]:NAME=VALUE`, where KIND is `txt`|`mx`|`cname`|`a` and MODE is `exact` (default) | `contains` | `prefix` (`contains`/`prefix` are TXT only). Needs a server built with `domain-verify-dns` and a `system·admin` token

**Usage:** `boatramp domain verify-records [OPTIONS] <HOST>`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<HOST>` | — | — | — | Host this record set belongs to (operator context; records name themselves) |
| `-r, --record <SPEC>` | — | — | — | A record spec `KIND[/MODE]:NAME=VALUE` (repeatable), e.g. `txt:_acme.example.com=tok`, `a:example.com=192.0.2.1`, `txt/contains:_dmarc.example.com=p=reject` |

## `boatramp token`

Manage control-plane API tokens

**Usage:** `boatramp token [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--server <SERVER>` | `BOATRAMP_SERVER` | — | — | boatramp server base URL (overrides [deploy].server) |

### `boatramp token create`

Mint a new token (printed once — not recoverable)

**Usage:** `boatramp token create [OPTIONS] <LABEL>`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<LABEL>` | — | — | — | Human label for the token |
| `--role <ROLES>` | — | — | — | Role (repeatable): `<role>` (global) or `<role>:<site>` (scoped) — e.g. `admin`, `publisher:blog`, `viewer:blog` |
| `--ttl-secs <TTL_SECS>` | — | — | — | Optional time-to-live in seconds (omit for no expiry) |
| `--holder-pub <HOLDER_PUB>` | — | — | — | Make the token **delegatable**: embed this holder public key (`"<alg>:<hex>"`, from `boatramp auth init`) as the `cnf`, so the holder of the matching private key can `token attenuate` it offline |
| `--pop` | — | — | — | Make the token **PoP-bound** (DPoP): generate a fresh holder keypair, mint the token against its public half (`cnf`), and print the holder **private** key as `BOATRAMP_TOKEN_HOLDER_KEY` so the client can sign a per-request proof. A leaked token alone is then inert without this key. Also set `BOATRAMP_POP_ORIGIN` to the server's `[serve] pop_origin` |

### `boatramp token bootstrap`

Mint the FIRST control-plane token on a fresh deploy by presenting the single-use bootstrap secret (`BOATRAMP_BOOTSTRAP_SECRET`) — no admin token needed. The server mints via its own root key (nothing sensitive leaves it) and records the token (revocable). Use it to configure + mint scoped tokens, then unset the secret on the server

**Usage:** `boatramp token bootstrap [OPTIONS]`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--role <ROLES>` | — | — | — | Role for the bootstrap token (repeatable). Defaults to `admin` |
| `--ttl-secs <TTL_SECS>` | — | — | — | Optional time-to-live in seconds (default: 3600 = 1 h) |

### `boatramp token mint`

Mint a token **offline** — sign locally via the configured signer (local key or KMS/HSM), no server. The key-holder's recovery / air-gap path; prefer `token bootstrap` for the normal first-token flow. The token is unlisted (no server round-trip records it) but still revocable by its id

**Usage:** `boatramp token mint [OPTIONS]`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--role <ROLES>` | — | — | — | Role (repeatable): `<role>` (global) or `<role>:<site>` (scoped) |
| `--ttl-secs <TTL_SECS>` | — | — | — | Optional time-to-live in seconds (omit for no expiry) |
| `--holder-pub <HOLDER_PUB>` | — | — | — | Make it delegatable: embed this holder public key (`"<alg>:<hex>"`) as the `cnf` so it can be narrowed with `token attenuate` |
| `--config <CONFIG>` | — | `boatramp.cfg` | — | `boatramp.cfg` supplying the signer (`[serve.signer]` / `auth_root_private_key`). Ignored when `BOATRAMP_AUTH_ROOT_PRIVATE_KEY` is set in the environment |

### `boatramp token attenuate`

Narrow a (delegatable) token **offline** — no server, no root key — by signing a restrict-only delegation block with the holder key. The result is a longer credential; present it in place of the original

**Usage:** `boatramp token attenuate [OPTIONS] <CREDENTIAL>`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<CREDENTIAL>` | — | — | — | The token / credential to narrow |
| `--holder-key <HOLDER_KEY>` | `BOATRAMP_HOLDER_KEY` | — | — | The holder private key (`"<alg>:<hex>"`) that the parent block's `cnf` authorized |
| `--only-site <ONLY_SITE>` | — | — | — | Restrict to a single site (denies every other target) |
| `--read-only` | — | — | — | Restrict to read-only operations |
| `--not-after <NOT_AFTER>` | — | — | — | Shorten the lifetime to this Unix second |
| `--next-holder-pub <NEXT_HOLDER_PUB>` | — | — | — | Permit one further attenuation by this holder public key (`"<alg>:<hex>"`); omit to make this the last block |

### `boatramp token ls`

List issued tokens (short id, label, roles, expiry)

**Usage:** `boatramp token ls`

### `boatramp token rm`

Revoke a token by its id or a unique id prefix

**Usage:** `boatramp token rm <ID>`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<ID>` | — | — | — | Token id (or prefix) |

| `--file <PATH>` | — | — | — | Read the plaintext from a file |
| `--value <VALUE>` | — | — | — | The plaintext inline. Convenient, but it lands in your shell history and the process table — prefer `--stdin` or `--file` for anything sensitive |

### `boatramp tenancy test-extract`

Dry-run a `token`-source claim transform against a sample claim value, **locally** (no server), through the SAME `derive_tenant` the host runs. Prints the derived tenant key, or the exact stage that denied it (the same deny taxonomy the host logs) — so a regex/template misconfiguration is a 30-second check instead of staring at silently fail-closed requests

**Usage:** `boatramp tenancy test-extract [OPTIONS]`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `--template <TEMPLATE>` | — | — | — | A `{tenant}`/`{_}` path template (the recommended surface) |
| `--regex <REGEX>` | — | — | — | A single-named-capture regex `(?<tenant>…)` (the escape hatch) |
| `--namespace <NAMESPACE>` | — | — | — | The optional per-issuer namespace (produces `<namespace>:<extracted>`) |

## `boatramp email`

Manage a project's SMTP delivery profiles (`email set|ls|show|rm`)

**Usage:** `boatramp email [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--server <SERVER>` | `BOATRAMP_SERVER` | — | — | boatramp server base URL (overrides [publish].server) |

### `boatramp email set`

Create or **update** an SMTP profile. Fields you pass overwrite; fields you omit keep their stored value — so you can change one parameter (e.g. `--from`) without re-sending the rest, and the sealed password is preserved unless you pass a new one. On create, `--host` and `--from` are required

**Usage:** `boatramp email set [OPTIONS] <NAME>`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<NAME>` | — | — | — | The profile name (a guest selects it via the message's `profile`; omit in the guest to use `default`) |
| `--host <HOST>` | — | — | — | SMTP relay hostname (required on create; omit to keep on update) |
| `--port <PORT>` | — | — | — | SMTP relay port; omit to keep (on create, the conventional port for `--security`: 587 starttls / 465 tls / 25 plaintext) |
| `--security <SECURITY>` | — | — | — | Transport security: `starttls` (587), `tls` (implicit, 465), or `plaintext` (a trusted local relay only). Omit to keep (defaults to `starttls` on create) |
| `--username <USERNAME>` | — | — | — | SMTP AUTH username. Omit to keep; use `--no-auth` to drop it |
| `--password <PASSWORD>` | — | — | — | The SMTP AUTH password inline. Convenient, but it lands in your shell history and the process table — prefer `--password-stdin` for anything sensitive |
| `--password-stdin` | — | — | — | Read the SMTP AUTH password from standard input (preferred) |
| `--no-auth` | — | — | — | Drop the username + password (an unauthenticated relay) |
| `--from <FROM>` | — | — | — | The default (and only permitted) `From` address (required on create; omit to keep) |
| `--durable <DURABLE>` | — | — | true \| false | Default sends through this profile to the durable spool (`--durable` = on, `--durable false` = off); omit to keep. A guest can still opt in/out per message |

### `boatramp email ls`

List the project's SMTP profiles (redacted — never the password)

**Usage:** `boatramp email ls`

Show one profile's redacted config

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<NAME>` | — | — | — | The profile name |

Remove a profile by name

**Usage:** `boatramp email rm <NAME>`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<NAME>` | — | — | — | The profile name |

## `boatramp cluster`

Operate a self-hosted cluster's mesh membership (mint join tokens)

**Usage:** `boatramp cluster [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--server <SERVER>` | `BOATRAMP_SERVER` | — | — | boatramp server base URL (overrides [deploy].server) |

### `boatramp cluster add`

Print a one-paste **join ticket** for a new node: a single-use join token bundled with the seed address + the cluster root anchor, so the joiner self-identifies and joins with no peer map. Run against any existing node

**Usage:** `boatramp cluster add [OPTIONS]`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--root-pubkey <ROOT_PUBKEY>` | — | — | — | The cluster **root public key** (`es256:`/`ed25519:` hex) — the anchor the joiner verifies the seed + members against. From `auth pubkey` |
| `--seed <SEED>` | — | — | — | The seed control-plane address the joiner should reach (defaults to `--server`). This is where the joiner POSTs its `/api/cluster/join` |
| `--ttl-secs <TTL_SECS>` | — | — | — | Token time-to-live in seconds (default: the server's short window) |
| `--print-token-only` | — | — | — | Print only the raw single-use token (scripting escape hatch), not the full ticket |

### `boatramp cluster join-token`

Mint a single-use **bearer** mesh join token (printed once). Any node can redeem it, but only by proving possession of its own mesh key at join time, and only once — hand it to exactly one joining node. (Prefer `cluster add`, which bundles the token into a one-paste join ticket.)

**Usage:** `boatramp cluster join-token [OPTIONS]`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--ttl-secs <TTL_SECS>` | — | — | — | Token time-to-live in seconds (default: the server's short window) |

### `boatramp cluster status`

Show the cluster membership — address-primary: ADDRESS, ROLE, a short node-id label, and STATE (ready/lagging). Target the leader for accurate learner catch-up

**Usage:** `boatramp cluster status [OPTIONS]`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--full` | — | — | — | Show full node ids instead of the short 8-hex label |

### `boatramp cluster promote`

Promote a caught-up learner to a **voter** (adds it to the quorum). The target is a **mesh address** (as shown by `status`) or a raw node id. Target the leader's API. Use this to build a voting quorum on bare metal (in Kubernetes the operator promotes automatically)

**Usage:** `boatramp cluster promote <TARGET>`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<TARGET>` | — | — | — | The node to promote: its mesh address (preferred) or its raw node id |

### `boatramp cluster rotate-key`

Rotate the `--server` node's own mesh key, make-before-break. Node-local: rotation happens on the node whose API you target (only it holds and mints its private key), so this rotates that node's key

**Usage:** `boatramp cluster rotate-key`

### `boatramp cluster remove`

Remove a node from the cluster (subsumes `revoke`): its trust is deleted cluster-wide (it can no longer authenticate) and it is dropped from the quorum. The target is a **mesh address** (as shown by `status`) or a raw node id. Target the leader's API so the quorum change applies

**Usage:** `boatramp cluster remove <TARGET>`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<TARGET>` | — | — | — | The node to remove: its mesh address (preferred) or its raw node id |

### `boatramp cluster revoke`

Revoke a node from the mesh by raw node id (low-level; prefer `remove`, which accepts an address). Target the leader's API

**Usage:** `boatramp cluster revoke <NODE>`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<NODE>` | — | — | — | The node id to revoke |

Resolve a `--tls rpk` server's TLS pin from your **root** public key: fetch the root-signed bootstrap attestation, verify it, and print the `BOATRAMP_SERVER_PUBKEY` to export — so you pin only the one root anchor and learn each node's TLS identity from its attestation

Print the active policy as JSON (the built-in default if none is stored)

Replace the policy from a JSON file (validated server-side before store)

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<FILE>` | — | — | — | Path to the policy JSON (matching `AuthzPolicy`) |

### `boatramp auth rotate-root`

**Rotate the cluster root key**, make-before-break. With no flag, list the extra trusted anchors. `--add` trusts a new anchor cluster-wide (so both old + new verify — no window where a valid token is rejected); re-point `[serve.signer]` to the new key so new tokens/attestations use it, then `--retire` the old anchor once every node has the new one. See `how-to/migrate-root-key.md`

**Usage:** `boatramp auth rotate-root [OPTIONS]`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--add <PUBKEY>` | — | — | — | Trust a new root anchor (`<alg>:<hex>` public key, from `auth pubkey`) |
| `--retire <PUBKEY>` | — | — | — | Retire a previously-added anchor (the old key, after propagation) |

### `boatramp gateway upstream`

Manage upstreams (declared backends)

#### `boatramp gateway upstream add`

Declare or replace an upstream. Give a single positional `target`, a pool of `--backend` URLs, or `--discover-host`/`--discover-port` for a DNS-discovered pool

**Usage:** `boatramp gateway upstream add [OPTIONS] <NAME> [TARGET]`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<NAME>` | — | — | — | Upstream name (referenced by routes) |
| `[TARGET]` | — | — | — | Single backend `scheme://host:port[/base]` (host may be private). Omit when using `--backend` or `--discover-host` |
| `--backend <URL>` | — | — | — | Pool backend URL (repeatable) — load-balanced across the pool. Supersedes the positional `target` |
| `--lb <LB>` | — | `round-robin` | round-robin \| random \| nearest | Load-balancing policy across the pool |
| `--max-retries <MAX_RETRIES>` | — | `0` | — | Extra backends to try on a connect failure (body-less requests only) |
| `--health-max-fails <HEALTH_MAX_FAILS>` | — | — | — | Eject a backend after this many consecutive failures (with `--health-timeout-ms`) |
| `--health-timeout-ms <HEALTH_TIMEOUT_MS>` | — | — | — | How long an ejected backend stays out (milliseconds) |
| `--probe-path <PROBE_PATH>` | — | — | — | Enable **active** health probing with this probe path (e.g. `/healthz`); the other `--probe-*` flags tune it |
| `--probe-interval-ms <PROBE_INTERVAL_MS>` | — | — | — | Active-probe interval (ms) |
| `--probe-timeout-ms <PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS>` | — | — | — | Active-probe timeout (ms) |
| `--probe-unhealthy-threshold <PROBE_UNHEALTHY_THRESHOLD>` | — | — | — | Consecutive failed probes before a backend leaves rotation |
| `--probe-healthy-threshold <PROBE_HEALTHY_THRESHOLD>` | — | — | — | Consecutive OK probes before a down backend returns |
| `--probe-expected-status <PROBE_EXPECTED_STATUS>` | — | — | — | HTTP status a healthy probe must return |
| `--discover-host <DISCOVER_HOST>` | — | — | — | DNS-discover the pool: resolve this host's A/AAAA records |
| `--discover-port <DISCOVER_PORT>` | — | — | — | Port for DNS-discovered backends |
| `--discover-scheme <DISCOVER_SCHEME>` | — | `http` | — | Scheme for DNS-discovered backends |
| `--discover-refresh-secs <DISCOVER_REFRESH_SECS>` | — | `30` | — | Re-resolve the discovered pool at most this often (seconds) |
| `--host-header <HOST_HEADER>` | — | — | — | Override the `Host` header sent upstream |
| `--strip-prefix <STRIP_PREFIX>` | — | — | — | Strip this path prefix before forwarding (`/app` → upstream `/`) |
| `--connect-timeout-ms <CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS>` | — | — | — | Connect timeout (milliseconds) |
| `--request-timeout-ms <REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS>` | — | — | — | Overall request timeout (milliseconds) |
| `--tls-insecure` | — | — | — | Accept a self-signed / invalid upstream TLS certificate |
| `--read-buffer-bytes <READ_BUFFER_BYTES>` | — | — | — | Cap the per-connection upstream read buffer (bytes); default 32768. Higher trades memory for fewer read syscalls (throughput on large responses); lower trades syscalls for less memory. Matters most at high proxy concurrency |
| `--client-region-header <CLIENT_REGION_HEADER>` | — | — | — | For `--lb nearest`: the request header carrying the client's region (set by the CDN/edge, e.g. `fly-region`, `cf-ipcountry`) |
| `--region <URL=REGION>` | — | — | — | For `--lb nearest`: tag a backend with a region as `URL=REGION` (repeatable). Untagged backends are region-neutral |

| `--replicas <REPLICAS>` | — | `1` | — | Desired replica count |
| `--entrypoint <ENTRYPOINT>` | — | — | — | In-guest entrypoint argv (repeatable) |
| `--env <ENV>` | — | — | — | Environment variable `K=V` (repeatable) |
| `--restart <RESTART>` | — | `always` | never \| on-failure \| always | Restart policy |
| `--scale-to-zero` | — | — | — | Snapshot + stop when idle; restore on the next request |
| `--startup-grace-secs <STARTUP_GRACE_SECS>` | — | — | — | Seconds a freshly launched replica has to become healthy before the reconcile loop treats a still-unhealthy replica as a broken launch to stop + relaunch. Raise it for a slow-initializing image (a stock database's first `initdb`) so it isn't killed mid-init. Omit for the default (30) |
| `--writable-root` | — | — | — | Allow a writable root filesystem (honored only under the single-tenant posture; the hardened read-only root is the default). Prefer a persistent volume for app writes |
| `--cap-add <CAP_ADD>` | — | — | — | Add back a Linux capability on the shared-kernel backends (docker / native container), without the `CAP_` prefix, e.g. `CHOWN` (repeatable). Honored only under the single-tenant posture. For an image whose entrypoint needs a capability (a stock database that `chown`s its data dir and drops privileges). Prefer `--user` + a persistent volume where the image allows |
| `--user <USER>` | — | — | — | Run the entrypoint as this user (`uid` or `uid:gid`, numeric) instead of the backend default, so a stock image can run rootless against a pre-owned volume — no added capabilities. Honored under any posture |
| `--isolation <ISOLATION>` | — | `trusted` | trusted \| untrusted | Isolation the workload requires (`trusted` allows containers; `untrusted` forces a microVM / managed platform) |
| `--region <REGIONS>` | — | — | — | Allowed region (repeatable; empty = any) |
| `--bind <BIND>` | — | — | — | Managed binding the workload depends on, `<kind>[:<name>]` (repeatable): `sql` binds the site database, `sql:analytics` a named external DB; `kv` binds the site key/value store, `kv:cache` one named bucket; `blob` binds the site blob store, `blob:assets` one named container; `messaging` binds the project bus — BOTH halves, publish AND consume (claim/ack/nack) — `messaging:deliver` one topic. The endpoint URL + token are injected into the guest env (`BOATRAMP_SQL_URL` / `BOATRAMP_KV_URL` / `BOATRAMP_BLOB_URL` / `BOATRAMP_MESSAGING_URL`). NOTE: a bare `kv`/`blob` (no `:<name>`) is SITE-WIDE — the workload can read/write EVERY bucket/container in its site's `hkv{,blob}/{site}/` space; use `kv:<name>` / `blob:<name>` to confine it. Likewise a bare `messaging` is PROJECT-BUS-WIDE (any topic under `{project}/bus/`, for both publish and claim); use `messaging:<topic>` to confine it to one topic. `invoke` (compute→function) is declared only — no shim resolver yet, so it parses but injects no env (Phase 3) |
| `--pull-secret <PULL_SECRET>` | — | — | — | Name of a **sealed registry pull credential** in THIS project's secret store for a private `--image` pull (set it first with `boatramp compute registry-auth set <name> --username … --password-stdin`). The host unseals it and authenticates the image pull at launch; a missing/unauthorized credential fails the pull CLOSED (never an anonymous fallback). Only meaningful with `--image`. Omit for a public image (or when an operator node-wide credential covers the registry host) |

| `--writable-root` | — | — | — | Allow a writable root filesystem (single-tenant posture only; the hardened read-only root is the default). Prefer a persistent volume |

| `--user <USER>` | — | — | — | Run the entrypoint as this user (`uid` or `uid:gid`, numeric) instead of the backend default. Lets a stock image run rootless against a pre-owned volume |

### `boatramp compute exec`

Run a command inside a running workload replica (docker-exec style) — e.g. pipe a SQL file into `psql`, or run `pg_dump`. Requires the server's `allow_compute_exec` posture; container + docker backends only. The command's stdout/stderr are printed and this process exits with its exit code

**Usage:** `boatramp compute exec [OPTIONS] <NAME> <ARGV>`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<NAME>` | — | — | — | Workload name |
| `<ARGV>` | — | — | — | The command argv — everything after `--`, e.g. `-- psql -U app -d appdb` |
| `--stdin` | — | — | — | Feed this process's standard input to the command (pipe a file in) |

### `boatramp compute bind-blob`

Mint a blob-shim credential for a NON-managed local process (dev/CI) and print it as env — the blob analogue of `DATABASE_URL`. The process then reads/writes the SAME `--site` blob namespace a managed workload (or a `wasi:blobstore` handler) for that site sees, so a handler↔native-worker shared-blob round-trip can be exercised offline. Requires the server's `allow_dev_blob_bind` posture (on by default only in `dev`); System·Admin. Example: `eval "$(boatramp compute bind-blob --site mailroom --export)"`

**Usage:** `boatramp compute bind-blob [OPTIONS]`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--site <SITE>` | — | — | — | The site (the workload identity) whose blob namespace to bind |
| `--container <CONTAINER>` | — | — | — | Confine the credential to one container (`--bind blob:<container>`); omit for a site-wide credential |
| `--project <PROJECT>` | — | — | — | The project owning the blob namespace (default `default`) |
| `--export` | — | — | — | Prefix each line with `export ` so the output is `eval`-able in a shell |

### `boatramp compute bind-messaging`

Mint a messaging-shim credential for a NON-managed local process (dev/CI) and print it as env — the messaging analogue of `bind-blob` (#07) / `DATABASE_URL`. The credential covers BOTH halves of the SAME `{project}/bus/<topic>` project bus a managed `--bind messaging` workload (or a `wasi:messaging` handler) for that project reaches: the process can publish AND claim/ack/nack, so either a native-producer → consumer-function, or a function-producer → native-consumer, bus round-trip can be exercised offline. Requires the server's `allow_dev_messaging_bind` posture (on by default only in `dev`); System·Admin. Example: `eval "$(boatramp compute bind-messaging --topic deliver --export)"`

**Usage:** `boatramp compute bind-messaging [OPTIONS]`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--topic <TOPIC>` | — | — | — | Confine the credential to one topic (`--bind messaging:<topic>`); omit for a project-bus-wide credential (any topic under `{project}/bus/`) |
| `--project <PROJECT>` | — | — | — | The project owning the bus (default `default`) |
| `--export` | — | — | — | Prefix each line with `export ` so the output is `eval`-able in a shell |

Manage persistent volumes: list them (with in-use / orphaned status) and reclaim a decommissioned workload's volume. The safe flow is `compute rm <workload>` first (unregister → the reconcile loop stops it), then `compute volume rm <name>`

#### `boatramp compute volume ls`

List persistent volumes (NAME / SIZE / IN-USE)

#### `boatramp compute volume rm`

Remove a persistent volume by name. Refused if a registered workload still references it, unless `--force`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<NAME>` | — | — | — | Volume name |
| `--force` | — | — | — | Remove even when a registered workload's spec still references it (the disposable-data override). Prefer `compute rm <workload>` first |

### `boatramp compute status`

Show observed per-replica runtime state — the reconcile plane's X-ray: stored health, lifecycle phase, assigned IP:port, age vs startup grace, backend. This is the record the endpoint resolver reads, so `HEALTHY=false` on a `running`, endpoint-bearing replica is the "reachable but not served" signature. Node-global (every tenant on the node); admin-scoped

**Usage:** `boatramp compute status [WORKLOAD]`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `[WORKLOAD]` | — | — | — | Show only this workload's replicas (default: every workload) |

### `boatramp compute set-health`

Force one replica's stored health flag — the escape hatch when a recovered replica is stuck `healthy=false` and the endpoint resolver therefore won't serve it (the v0.3.12→v0.3.13 class), without waiting for a binary patch. Targets the `--project` tenant's workload. Node-global; admin-scoped

**Usage:** `boatramp compute set-health [OPTIONS] <WORKLOAD> <REPLICA>`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<WORKLOAD>` | — | — | — | Workload name |
| `<REPLICA>` | — | — | — | Replica ordinal |
| `--healthy <HEALTHY>` | — | — | true \| false | The health value to persist (`--healthy true` \| `--healthy false`) |

### `boatramp compute ip`

Inspect the compute IP plane (`ip ls`): every replica's assigned IP, with duplicate-IP collisions flagged. Node-global; admin-scoped

**Usage:** `boatramp compute ip <COMMAND>`

#### `boatramp compute ip ls`

List IP assignments (IP / OWNER / HEALTHY), flagging duplicate-IP collisions

**Usage:** `boatramp compute ip ls`

### `boatramp compute reconcile`

Force the reconcile loop to run a convergence pass now (the "kick it" lever for a workload stuck mid-reconcile) instead of waiting for the next periodic tick. Fire-and-forget — follow with `compute status` to see the result. Node-global; admin-scoped

**Usage:** `boatramp compute reconcile`

### `boatramp compute restart`

Restart one replica: stop it and let the reconcile loop relaunch a fresh one (re-running IP allocation) — the live workaround for a wedged replica or a stale IP assignment. Targets the `--project` tenant's workload. Node-global; admin-scoped

**Usage:** `boatramp compute restart <WORKLOAD> <REPLICA>`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<WORKLOAD>` | — | — | — | Workload name |
| `<REPLICA>` | — | — | — | Replica ordinal |

### `boatramp compute dns`

Inspect internal service discovery (`dns ls` / `dns resolve <workload>`): the name → healthy-replica-IP map a co-located guest resolves. Node-global; admin-scoped

**Usage:** `boatramp compute dns <COMMAND>`

#### `boatramp compute dns ls`

List internal names and the healthy replica IPs each resolves to

**Usage:** `boatramp compute dns ls`

#### `boatramp compute dns resolve`

Resolve one workload's internal name (in the `--project` tenant) to its healthy replica IPs — exactly as a same-project peer's lookup would

**Usage:** `boatramp compute dns resolve <WORKLOAD>`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<WORKLOAD>` | — | — | — | Workload name |

### `boatramp compute netdiag`

Actively probe a workload's replicas from the node — a TCP reachability check against each replica's endpoint, alongside its stored state. Answers "can the node actually reach this replica right now?"; `REACHABLE=yes` + `HEALTHY=no` is the reachable-but-not-served signature. Targets the `--project` tenant's workload. Node-global; admin-scoped

**Usage:** `boatramp compute netdiag <WORKLOAD>`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<WORKLOAD>` | — | — | — | Workload name |

### `boatramp compute registry-auth`

Manage **sealed registry pull credentials** for private `image(...)` workloads. Project-scoped by default (a credential in THIS project's secret store, referenced from `compute set --pull-secret <name>`); `--operator` manages the node-wide `[compute].registry_auth` host-map credentials instead (System·Admin). The password is sealed server-side and is never echoed back

**Usage:** `boatramp compute registry-auth <COMMAND>`

#### `boatramp compute registry-auth set`

Seal (or rotate) a registry credential under `name`. Project-scoped unless `--operator`. Setting an existing name rotates it

**Usage:** `boatramp compute registry-auth set [OPTIONS] <NAME>`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<NAME>` | — | — | — | The credential name. Project scope: the `--pull-secret <name>` a workload references. Operator scope: the ref used as a `[compute].registry_auth` value |
| `--username <USERNAME>` | — | — | — | The registry username |
| `--password-stdin` | — | — | — | Read the password/token from standard input (preferred: nothing hits argv/shell history) |
| `--password <PASSWORD>` | — | — | — | The password/token inline. Convenient, but it lands in your shell history and the process table — prefer `--password-stdin` |
| `--operator` | — | — | — | Manage the OPERATOR node-wide credential (System·Admin) instead of this project's. Matched to a registry host via `[compute].registry_auth` |

#### `boatramp compute registry-auth ls`

List registry credential names + metadata (never a value)

**Usage:** `boatramp compute registry-auth ls [OPTIONS]`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--operator` | — | — | — | List the OPERATOR node-wide credentials instead of this project's |

#### `boatramp compute registry-auth rm`

Remove a registry credential by name

**Usage:** `boatramp compute registry-auth rm [OPTIONS] <NAME>`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<NAME>` | — | — | — | The credential name |
| `--operator` | — | — | — | Remove an OPERATOR node-wide credential instead of this project's |

### `boatramp compute reap`

Reap stuck ORPHANED compute replicas — a replica with NO desired workload AND no live container that the reconcile plane ignores (it converges only against desired workloads). DESTRUCTIVE + node-global; admin-scoped. **Dry-run by default**: it reports what it WOULD reap and changes nothing unless `--execute` is passed. Fail- closed — it never reaps a replica that is live or part of a desired spec, even one you name explicitly. Name a `<workload>` + `--replica` to target one; omit both to scan every project

**Usage:** `boatramp compute reap [OPTIONS] [WORKLOAD]`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `[WORKLOAD]` | — | — | — | Reap only this workload's replica (requires `--replica`). Omit to scan all |
| `--replica <REPLICA>` | — | — | — | Replica ordinal (with `<workload>`) |
| `--execute` | — | — | — | Actually reap. Without this the command is a dry-run (report only) |
| `--reclaim-volumes` | — | — | — | Also delete the orphan's persistent volume staging (e.g. a stranded managed-PG PGDATA). Off by default — the record + container are reaped but data preserved |
| `--grace-secs <GRACE_SECS>` | — | — | — | Minimum orphan age (seconds) required before acting. Default 0 for an explicit target (the no-desired-workload + container-gone checks are the real guarantee) |

### `boatramp sql exec`

Apply a migration **script** (multiple statements — `CREATE EXTENSION`, tables, RLS, chained DDL/DML) to a managed database. Reads from `--file` or standard input

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--db <DB>` | — | `default` | — | The database binding name (`default` = the project's default database) |
| `--file <FILE>` | — | — | — | Read the script from this file instead of standard input |

Run one row-returning query against a managed database and print the result

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<SQL>` | — | — | — | The SQL query (a single statement) |
| `--db <DB>` | — | `default` | — | The database binding name (`default` = the project's default database) |

### `boatramp sql ping`

Actively probe each replica of a managed database — a TCP reachability check that BYPASSES the stored-health gate `query` trips on. Distinguishes "the DB is actually down" from "the DB is up but the resolver won't serve it" (`REACHABLE=yes` + `HEALTHY=no`). Admin-scoped

**Usage:** `boatramp sql ping [OPTIONS]`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--db <DB>` | — | `default` | — | The database binding name (`default` = the project's default database) |

### `boatramp sql move`

**Relocate** a site's libsql database, data intact — e.g. give the default database a real name, or move a named database. Local single-node only; a remote/sqld backend is refused. A destructive, admin-scoped maintenance op: it vacuums a consistent copy to the destination, verifies it, then removes the source. Refuses to overwrite an existing destination

**Usage:** `boatramp sql move [OPTIONS]`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--db <DB>` | — | `default` | — | The **source** database binding name (`default` = the site's default database) |
| `--to <TO>` | — | — | — | The **destination** binding name (must be a valid, non-existing database name) |
| `--site <SITE>` | — | — | — | The site whose database is being relocated (falls back to `publish.site`) |

### `boatramp sql rehome-default`

**Default-scope re-home** a reserved-`default`-project site's libsql database (v0.31.0 Finding 8), OFFLINE + node-local — the libsql half of the `boatramp migrate` default-scope re-key. Copy-verifies the pre-fix bare `{dir}/{site}.db` to the post-fix `{dir}/default/{site}.db` (`VACUUM INTO` → `integrity_check` → remove source + WAL/SHM), data intact, then a reopen via `database("default", site, …)` resolves the new two-segment path

**Usage:** `boatramp sql rehome-default [OPTIONS]`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--site <SITE>` | — | — | — | The site whose default-project database is being re-homed |
| `--db <DB>` | — | `default` | — | The database binding name to re-home (`default` = the site's default database) |
| `--node-config <NODE_CONFIG>` | — | `boatramp.cfg` | — | Path to the node config (`boatramp.cfg` shape) whose `handlers.bindings.sql` + `[serve]` data_dir locate the libsql store. Defaults to `boatramp.cfg` |

Restart a managed database (`Project·Admin`): stop it so the reconcile loop relaunches it, applying any restart-requiring config change staged on the declaration in the process (e.g. a flipped `delta_capture`, which needs `wal_level=logical`/`--log-bin` in the launch argv to take effect). The explicit restart path a `restart_policy: manual` config change needs (see `db status`'s "pending restart" signal), and a general lever to bounce a database that needs no config change at all

## `boatramp kv`

Maintain the control-plane SlateDB store (`kv repair` — recover a torn WAL tail after a crash/snapshot; dry-run by default, `--apply` to perform it)

**Usage:** `boatramp kv <COMMAND>`

### `boatramp kv repair`

Repair a torn TRAILING WAL tail on the control-plane SlateDB store so it opens again (crash / snapshot partial-tail recovery). DRY-RUN by default (prints the plan); pass `--apply` to quarantine the torn tail. Refuses on a mid-range gap or unreadable manifest. This is the OFFLINE tail-only quarantine; `boatramp kv recover` is the daemon-mediated superset (in-place robust repair, else adopt a clean volume)

**Usage:** `boatramp kv repair [OPTIONS]`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--kv <BACKEND>` | `BOATRAMP_KV` | `slatedb` | slatedb \| memory \| cloudflare \| sql | Which control-plane KV backend this node runs (matches `serve --kv` / `BOATRAMP_KV`). These `boatramp kv` verbs are SlateDB maintenance/recovery tools (manifest / WAL / `.compactions`); they do NOT apply to a `sql` backend (the SQL engine's own crash recovery handles that), nor to `memory` / `cloudflare`. A non-SlateDB backend gets a clear "not applicable" message rather than building a bogus SlateDB object store against a path that isn't one |

| `--kv-s3` | `BOATRAMP_KV_S3` | — | — | Target the R2/S3-backed store instead of the local disk store (matches `serve --kv-s3`). Uses the ambient AWS credentials; addressing comes from the `--s3-*` flags below |
| `--s3-bucket <S3_BUCKET>` | `BOATRAMP_S3_BUCKET` | — | — | S3/R2 bucket for `--kv-s3` |
| `--s3-endpoint <S3_ENDPOINT>` | `BOATRAMP_S3_ENDPOINT` | — | — | S3/R2 endpoint for `--kv-s3` (R2: `https://<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com`) |
| `--s3-region <S3_REGION>` | `BOATRAMP_S3_REGION` | — | — | S3/R2 region for `--kv-s3` (R2 uses `auto`) |
| `--s3-path-style` | `BOATRAMP_S3_PATH_STYLE` | — | — | Path-style addressing for `--kv-s3` (R2 accepts it) |
| `--kv-s3-prefix <KV_S3_PREFIX>` | `BOATRAMP_KV_S3_PREFIX` | `_kv` | — | Key prefix (root) of the `--kv-s3` store within the bucket (matches `serve --kv-s3-prefix`) |
| `--apply` | — | — | — | Perform the quarantine. Without this the command is a DRY-RUN: it prints the plan and mutates NOTHING |

### `boatramp kv checkpoint`

Flush the control-plane store to a consistent, GUARANTEED-BOOTABLE on-disk state (drain WAL→L0, advance the durable frontier), so an operator can snapshot the volume safely. OFFLINE by default (the daemon must be stopped — SlateDB is single-writer). Pass `--live` to checkpoint a RUNNING daemon over `POST /api/kv-checkpoint` (System·Admin) WITHOUT stopping it — the client verb for the on-demand live checkpoint (the automatic form is the `[serve.kv] checkpoint_interval` cadence). The offline form fails loud if the store is torn (run `kv recover` first). NOTE (fsync): a snapshot is bootable only after a checkpoint drained WAL→L0; v0.11.0 fsync makes even a mid-close hard stop non-corrupting, but a checkpoint before the snapshot is still the reliable point-in-time

### `boatramp kv recover`

Recover an unbootable control-plane store (v0.9.0 KV-recovery, C9/C10) — the SUPERSET of `kv repair`. DRY-RUN by default (diagnose the WHOLE store + print the plan). `--apply` repairs a recoverable shape IN PLACE (quarantine a safe trailing torn tail, retaining the torn bytes for forensics). For an UNSAFE shape (a torn compacted/L0 SST), attach a clean volume snapshot and pass `--adopt-volume <mounted-path>`: it validates the attached store opens clean + zero-torn BEFORE adopting, prints the discard-delta, and (with `--apply`) adopts it via verify-open-then-swap, RETAINING the crashed copy until the adopt is verified

**Usage:** `boatramp kv recover [OPTIONS]`

These `boatramp kv` verbs are SlateDB maintenance/recovery tools (manifest / WAL / `.compactions`); they do NOT apply to a `sql` backend (the SQL engine's own crash recovery handles that), nor to `memory` / `cloudflare`. A non-SlateDB backend gets a clear "not applicable" message rather than building a bogus SlateDB object store against a path that isn't one |
| `--data-dir <DATA_DIR>` | — | `./data` | — | The server data directory (as passed to `boatramp serve --data-dir`). The local SlateDB control-plane store lives under `<data-dir>/kv-slate` (root `kv`). Defaults to `./data` |

| `--s3-bucket <S3_BUCKET>` | `BOATRAMP_S3_BUCKET` | — | — | S3/R2 bucket for `--kv-s3` |
| `--s3-endpoint <S3_ENDPOINT>` | `BOATRAMP_S3_ENDPOINT` | — | — | S3/R2 endpoint for `--kv-s3` (R2: `https://<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com`) |
| `--s3-region <S3_REGION>` | `BOATRAMP_S3_REGION` | — | — | S3/R2 region for `--kv-s3` (R2 uses `auto`) |
| `--s3-path-style` | `BOATRAMP_S3_PATH_STYLE` | — | — | Path-style addressing for `--kv-s3` (R2 accepts it) |
| `--kv-s3-prefix <KV_S3_PREFIX>` | `BOATRAMP_KV_S3_PREFIX` | `_kv` | — | Key prefix (root) of the `--kv-s3` store within the bucket (matches `serve --kv-s3-prefix`) |
| `--apply` | — | — | — | Perform the recovery (in-place repair, or adopt the attached volume). Without this the command is a DRY-RUN: it diagnoses + prints the plan and mutates NOTHING |
| `--adopt-volume <MOUNTED_PATH>` | — | — | — | Adopt an operator-attached CLEAN volume snapshot mounted at this path (expects its `kv-slate` store underneath) INSTEAD of an in-place repair — for a shape beyond auto-heal (a torn compacted/L0 SST). The attached store is validated (opens clean + zero-torn) BEFORE adopting; `--apply` swaps it in, RETAINING the crashed copy until the adopt is verified. boatramp does NOT create/destroy fly volumes — attach the snapshot volume with the fly CLI first (`fly volumes create` from a snapshot, then mount it). Local-disk / fly-volume only |

### `boatramp kv export`

Export the control-plane KV to a PORTABLE, backend-agnostic dump FILE (kv-sql WS7). A LOGICAL dump captures CONTENT (`{key, value, version}` records), NOT the physical LSM/manifest/ `.compactions` — so a restore (`kv import`) rebuilds a FRESH clean store, structurally immune to the torn-manifest / corrupt-`.compactions` physical-corruption classes that make volume snapshots useless. Works over ANY backend. The dump carries SEALED ciphertext for secrets (sealing is pre-put — NO plaintext) + plaintext control-plane config/RBAC, and NEVER the envelope KEK (a restore needs the separately-held key). OFFLINE/quiesced by default (the daemon should be stopped — a live single-writer source races concurrent writes). SENSITIVE — op-gated over the API (`GET /api/kv-export`, System·Admin); protect the file at rest

**Usage:** `boatramp kv export [OPTIONS]`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--store <STORE>` | — | `slatedb:./data` | — | The KV endpoint to export (see the subcommand help for the descriptor forms). Defaults to the local SlateDB store under `./data/kv-slate` |
| `--out <FILE>` | — | — | — | Write the portable dump to this file (the sensitive dump — protect it at rest) |

### `boatramp kv import`

Import a portable dump FILE (from `kv export`) into a control-plane KV (kv-sql WS7). DRY-RUN by default (prints the plan: source key count, destination state, what would be copied); `--apply` executes, then VERIFIES (re-reads every key, compares bytes + count). REFUSES a non-empty destination — or one with an existing control-plane identity — unless `--force` (never silently COMMINGLE two control planes). The reserved `_cp/*` / `_inval/*` feeds are never imported (they regenerate). OFFLINE/quiesced by default

**Usage:** `boatramp kv import [OPTIONS] <FILE>`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<FILE>` | — | — | — | The portable dump file to import (produced by `kv export` / `GET /api/kv-export`) |
| `--store <STORE>` | — | `slatedb:./data` | — | The destination KV endpoint (see the subcommand help). Defaults to the local SlateDB store |
| `--apply` | — | — | — | Perform the import. Without this the command is a DRY-RUN: it prints the plan and mutates NOTHING |
| `--force` | — | — | — | Overlay the dump onto a NON-EMPTY destination (or one with an existing control-plane identity). Without it, a non-empty destination is REFUSED to avoid commingling two control planes |

### `boatramp kv migrate`

Migrate a control-plane KV store→store over the portable dump (kv-sql WS7) — the SlateDB⇄SQL adoption path (and back). DRY-RUN by default (prints the plan); `--apply` copies + VERIFIES (bytes + count). REFUSES a non-empty `--to` destination unless `--force`. Reserved `_cp/*` / `_inval/*` feeds are skipped (regenerated). OFFLINE/quiesced by default

**Usage:** `boatramp kv migrate [OPTIONS]`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--from <DESCRIPTOR>` | — | — | — | The SOURCE KV endpoint (see the subcommand help for the descriptor forms) |
| `--to <DESCRIPTOR>` | — | — | — | The DESTINATION KV endpoint |
| `--apply` | — | — | — | Perform the migration. Without this the command is a DRY-RUN: it prints the plan and mutates NOTHING |
| `--force` | — | — | — | Overlay onto a NON-EMPTY `--to` destination (or one with an existing control-plane identity). Without it, a non-empty destination is REFUSED (commingle hazard) |

### `boatramp kv stats`

Report the control-plane SlateDB store's PHYSICAL vs LOGICAL size (kv-data-observability) — the diagnostic the 17.2 GB ENOSPC incident lacked. PHYSICAL = a walk of every object under the store root (live AND superseded SSTs, every manifest version, every WAL object), broken down per subdir (`wal/`, `compacted/`, `manifest/`, `compactions/`). LOGICAL = the bytes the CURRENT manifest actually references (live SSTs). The gap is reclaimable garbage — `boatramp kv compact` reclaims it. Pure read-only; safe against a quiesced store

### `boatramp kv compact`

Compact + garbage-collect the control-plane SlateDB store to reclaim the physical-vs-logical gap (kv-data-observability). DRY-RUN by default (prints the physical/logical stats + the reclaimable delta, and runs GC in dry-run so slatedb logs the delete candidates — mutates NOTHING). `--apply` performs a one-shot FULL MERGE of every L0 SST + sorted run into one sorted run, then GCs the now-unreferenced garbage (superseded SSTs + old manifests + replayed WAL). GC deletion is IRREVERSIBLE. OFFLINE ONLY: STOP the daemon first — SlateDB is single-writer (manifest fencing) and a running daemon runs its own embedded compactor + GC, which this would contend. Like `kv repair` / `kv recover`, it addresses `<data-dir>/kv-slate` directly

**Usage:** `boatramp kv compact [OPTIONS]`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--kv <BACKEND>` | `BOATRAMP_KV` | `slatedb` | slatedb \| memory \| cloudflare \| sql | Which control-plane KV backend this node runs (matches `serve --kv` / `BOATRAMP_KV`). These `boatramp kv` verbs are SlateDB maintenance/recovery tools (manifest / WAL / `.compactions`); they do NOT apply to a `sql` backend (the SQL engine's own crash recovery handles that), nor to `memory` / `cloudflare`. A non-SlateDB backend gets a clear "not applicable" message rather than building a bogus SlateDB object store against a path that isn't one |
| `--data-dir <DATA_DIR>` | — | `./data` | — | The server data directory (as passed to `boatramp serve --data-dir`). The local SlateDB control-plane store lives under `<data-dir>/kv-slate` (root `kv`). Defaults to `./data` |
| `--kv-s3` | `BOATRAMP_KV_S3` | — | — | Target the R2/S3-backed store instead of the local disk store (matches `serve --kv-s3`). Uses the ambient AWS credentials; addressing comes from the `--s3-*` flags below |
| `--s3-bucket <S3_BUCKET>` | `BOATRAMP_S3_BUCKET` | — | — | S3/R2 bucket for `--kv-s3` |
| `--s3-endpoint <S3_ENDPOINT>` | `BOATRAMP_S3_ENDPOINT` | — | — | S3/R2 endpoint for `--kv-s3` (R2: `https://<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com`) |
| `--s3-region <S3_REGION>` | `BOATRAMP_S3_REGION` | — | — | S3/R2 region for `--kv-s3` (R2 uses `auto`) |
| `--s3-path-style` | `BOATRAMP_S3_PATH_STYLE` | — | — | Path-style addressing for `--kv-s3` (R2 accepts it) |
| `--kv-s3-prefix <KV_S3_PREFIX>` | `BOATRAMP_KV_S3_PREFIX` | `_kv` | — | Key prefix (root) of the `--kv-s3` store within the bucket (matches `serve --kv-s3-prefix`) |
| `--apply` | — | — | — | Perform the compaction + GC reclaim. Without this the command is a DRY-RUN: it prints the physical/logical stats and the reclaimable delta, runs GC in dry-run (slatedb logs the delete candidates), and mutates NOTHING. `--apply` runs the full-merge compaction then the IRREVERSIBLE GC. OFFLINE ONLY — stop the daemon first |
| `--timeout-secs <SECONDS>` | — | `3600` | — | Max seconds to wait for the full-merge compaction to land before stopping the compactor (a large store merges a lot of data). Default 3600 (1 hour). Only used with `--apply` |
