### `boatramp blob mint-upload`

Mint a scoped, short-lived S3 upload credential for a project+site's blob container, which an external client (a browser, a bulk agent) uses to upload directly over the S3 protocol. The wasm guest then reads the object by key via the unchanged `wasi:blobstore`. Project is host-forced from your token/`--project`; the TTL + max-bytes are clamped to the operator ceilings. Gated by an operator token holding the `BlobUpload` right

**Usage:** `boatramp blob mint-upload [OPTIONS]`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--site <SITE>` | — | — | — | The site the container belongs to (with the host-forced project, scopes the credential) |
| `-c, --container <CONTAINER>` | — | — | — | The blob container to mint an upload credential for |
| `--key <KEY>` | — | — | — | Bind the credential to exactly ONE object key (the browser-UGC shape; create-only by default) |
| `--prefix <PREFIX>` | — | — | — | Bind the credential to a key PREFIX (the bulk-agent shape; needs an S3 SDK) |
| `--perms <PERMS>` | — | — | — | Permitted operations (repeatable): `put` (single-shot) and/or `multipart` (resumable). Empty ⇒ write-only (single-shot) |
| `--ttl <TTL>` | — | `900` | — | Credential lifetime in seconds (clamped to the operator ceiling) |
| `--content-type <CONTENT_TYPE>` | — | — | — | Constrain the uploaded object's Content-Type (exact, or a `type/*` family) |
| `--max-bytes <MAX_BYTES>` | — | — | — | Constrain the uploaded object's max size in bytes (clamped to the operator ceiling) |
| `--sha256` | — | — | — | Require content-addressing: the object key must equal `sha256(bytes)` (idempotent, replay-inert) |
| `--emit <EMIT>` | — | `human` | human \| env \| aws \| rclone \| json | Output form: `env` (a shell `export …` block for an S3 SDK), `aws` (an `~/.aws`-style profile), `rclone` (an rclone remote block), or `json` (the raw credential). Default ⇒ a human table plus an `env` block |

### `boatramp blob migrate`

**Migrate the node blob backend**, offline: copy every object from a SOURCE backend to a DESTINATION backend so switching `--blobs` (fs→cloud, provider→provider, region→region) has no re-upload step and no serving gap. This is a NODE-LOCAL operation — it builds both backends in-process from two node config files (`boatramp.cfg` shape: their `[serve]` blob block + optional `[secrets]`), NOT a control-plane HTTP call, so it needs local access to the backends' credentials, not a `BOATRAMP_SERVER`

**Usage:** `boatramp blob migrate [OPTIONS]`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--from <FROM>` | — | — | — | Path to the node config file (`boatramp.cfg` shape) whose `[serve]` blob block defines the SOURCE backend (+ optional `[secrets]` for a sealed `boatramp:`/`env:` S3 credential ref). OPTIONAL: when omitted, the SOURCE is the `[serve.blob_fallback]` SECONDARY of the node config (`--node-config`, default `boatramp.cfg`) — the zero-downtime drain one-liner. Omitting it with no configured fallback is an error |
| `--to <TO>` | — | — | — | Path to the node config file whose `[serve]` blob block defines the DESTINATION backend. OPTIONAL: when omitted, the DESTINATION defaults to the node config's OWN blob backend (the running node's primary), so `boatramp blob migrate --from <old>` migrates into the node you run |
| `--node-config <NODE_CONFIG>` | — | `boatramp.cfg` | — | Path to the running node's config (`boatramp.cfg` shape) — the source of the `--from`/`--to` defaults: its `[serve]` blob block is the DEFAULT destination (the primary), and its `[serve.blob_fallback]` is the DEFAULT source (the secondary). Only read when `--from` or `--to` is omitted. Defaults to `boatramp.cfg` |
| `--concurrency <CONCURRENCY>` | — | `8` | — | Bounded copy concurrency (number of objects in flight at once) |
| `--no-verify` | — | — | — | Skip the post-copy verification pass. Verification (every source object present in the destination) is ON by default; pass `--no-verify` to turn it off |
| `--dry-run` | — | — | — | Enumerate + classify (would-copy / would-skip) and report, but copy nothing |
| `--prefix <PREFIX>` | — | `` | — | Restrict the migration to source keys under this prefix (default: all objects) |

### `boatramp blob drain`

**Drain the daemon's configured `[serve.blob_fallback]`** secondary into the primary, over the control plane — for a MANAGED node reachable only via `BOATRAMP_SERVER` (no local disk / no `fly ssh`), where the offline `blob migrate` can't run. Unlike `blob migrate`, this REQUIRES a server: it triggers the RUNNING daemon (which already holds both backends of its `FallbackStorage` composite open) to copy its OWN configured secondary → primary internally, then relays progress

**Usage:** `boatramp blob drain [OPTIONS]`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--dry-run` | — | — | — | Enumerate + classify (would-copy / would-skip) on the daemon and report, but copy nothing |
| `--concurrency <CONCURRENCY>` | — | — | — | Bounded copy concurrency on the daemon (objects in flight at once) |
| `--prefix <PREFIX>` | — | — | — | Restrict the drain to secondary keys under this prefix (default: all objects) |

### `boatramp blob purge`

**Purge a PROVABLY-SAFE blob set** over the control plane (v0.6.4). Dry-run by default (report only); pass `--apply` to actually delete. Exactly ONE mode is required:

**Usage:** `boatramp blob purge [OPTIONS]`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--unreferenced` | — | — | — | Reclaim content-addressed blobs no live manifest references (on-demand GC). Refused (409) while a read-fallback secondary is attached |
| `--drained-source` | — | — | — | Reclaim the drained OLD secondary: delete each source key only once byte-confirmed in the primary (fail-closed). Requires a configured `[serve.blob_fallback]` |
| `--legacy-derivatives` | — | — | — | Drop stale image derivatives of a SUPERSEDED format (the pre-WEBP `.jpg` leftovers): delete ONLY `der/` objects of the `--superseded-ext` format under `--prefix`. A referenced baseline/primary (even with the same extension) and the current-format derivative are NEVER touched — a dropped derivative self-heals (regenerates on next access). Requires `--superseded-ext` |
| `--superseded-ext <EXT>` | — | — | — | The superseded image extension to drop (e.g. `jpg`), for `--legacy-derivatives` only |
| `--apply` | — | — | — | Actually delete (default: dry-run — report what WOULD be reclaimed, delete nothing) |
| `--prefix <PREFIX>` | — | — | — | Restrict a `--drained-source` / `--legacy-derivatives` purge to keys under this prefix (e.g. `hblob/<project>/`; default: all objects). Ignored by `--unreferenced` (which GCs the whole content-addressed keyspace) |

### `boatramp blob reconcile`

**Guarded reconcile** (System·Admin, PLAN-clone-robustness #4): repair an index↔object SIZE drift (a blob whose declared size disagrees with its stored bytes — what `blob verify` reports and what fail-closes a streaming clone) by "blessing" the stored bytes: re-write each in-scope object so the backend's declared size matches its body. DEFAULT-scoped to re-generable `der/` derivatives (safe — they self-heal); a baseline/primary reconcile blesses a possible truncation on load-bearing data, so it needs the explicit `--include-primary`. Dry-run by default (report-then-confirm); pass `--apply` to write

**Usage:** `boatramp blob reconcile [OPTIONS]`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--apply` | — | — | — | Actually re-write drifted objects (default: dry-run — report what WOULD be reconciled, write nothing). Report-then-confirm: run without this first, inspect the plan, then re-run with it |
| `--prefix <PREFIX>` | — | — | — | Restrict the scan to keys under this prefix (e.g. `hblob/<project>/`; default: all objects) |
| `--include-primary` | — | — | — | DANGEROUS, audited opt-in: also reconcile BASELINE/PRIMARY objects, not just re-generable `der/` derivatives. This blesses a truncation on load-bearing data (makes the index agree with possibly-corrupt bytes), so it is off by default — a primary-blob reconcile needs this explicit flag, and each such object is logged |

### `boatramp blob status`

Print the node's structured blob transition-mode state (v0.6.4): whether a read-fallback secondary is currently attached (the node is mid-migration). The direct, structured answer to "is this node still in TRANSITION mode?" — no log-grepping. Read-only (System·Read)

**Usage:** `boatramp blob status`

### `boatramp blob verify`

**Verify content-addressed references** (System·Read): list every blob a LIVE site deployment or function references that is MISSING from the backend — a dead reference that would 404 on invoke/serve (the `identity`-component-missing shape). Read-only. To repair one, re-upload the bytes (`boatramp blob put <file>`) or re-deploy the resource; the GC fix that stops new dead references (referencing live function components) ships alongside this

**Usage:** `boatramp blob verify`

### `boatramp blob rehome`

**Default-scope blob re-home** (v0.31.0 Finding 8), offline + node-local — the blob half of the `boatramp migrate` default-scope re-key. Re-homes the node's own bare default-scoped blob objects (`hblob/{site}/…`, `mqp/…`, `mqgp/…`) to their two-segment `…/default/…` spelling IN PLACE on the node's own backend (built from `--node-config`'s `[serve]` block, like `blob migrate`). It reads the `projectmeta/` project set from the control-plane KV so a named project's keys are never touched

**Usage:** `boatramp blob rehome [OPTIONS]`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--node-config <NODE_CONFIG>` | — | `boatramp.cfg` | — | Path to the running node's config (`boatramp.cfg` shape). Its `[serve]` blob block is the backend re-homed in place, and its `[serve].data_dir` locates the control-plane KV |
| `--kv <KV>` | — | `slatedb` | slatedb \| memory \| cloudflare \| sql | Metadata (KV) backend holding the `projectmeta/` project set. Must match `serve` |
| `--data-dir <DATA_DIR>` | — | — | — | Data directory for the control-plane KV (flag > `[serve].data_dir` > `./data`). Must match `serve` |
| `--finalize` | — | — | — | Finalize: delete each old bare-scoped key ONLY after its new `…/default/…` key verifies present (copy-before-delete). Without this the run is the non-destructive drain (copy + verify, keep old) |
| `--dry-run` | — | — | — | Classify/would-copy (drain) or would-delete (finalize) only; write + delete nothing |

## `boatramp migrate`

Migrate a pre-0.2.0 control-plane store to the project-scoped layout (`--dry-run` to preview; `--stage`/`--finalize` for a soak window)

**Usage:** `boatramp migrate [OPTIONS]`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--data-dir <DATA_DIR>` | `BOATRAMP_DATA_DIR` | — | — | Data directory (flag/env > `[serve].data_dir` > `./data`). Must match `serve` |
| `--kv <KV>` | — | `slatedb` | slatedb \| memory \| cloudflare \| sql | Metadata (KV) backend. Must match `serve` |
| `--dry-run` | — | — | — | Report what the migration would change, writing nothing |
| `--stage` | — | — | — | Copy + verify, keeping the old-layout keys for a soak/rollback window (the `dual` state). v0.31.0: this is now the DEFAULT behavior (the default-scope re-home MUST soak so the translating blob read-fallback engages), so the flag is accepted for clarity/compat but the forward pass always stages — a later `--finalize` reclaims the old keys |
| `--finalize` | — | — | — | Delete the old-layout keys left by the staged forward pass, completing the migration. For the default-scope re-home (v0.31.0 Finding 8) this REFUSES until the blob + libsql substrates are re-homed (it reads `--node-config` to check), because clearing the dual soak disengages the blob read-fallback |
| `--abort` | — | — | — | Abort a staged (dual-soak) migration, rolling the store back to its exact pre-forward bytes — the reverse of a `stage`. OFFLINE (run with the node stopped). Fail-closed: refuses, deleting nothing, if any staged key received a write during the soak (that write would be lost); finalize forward instead, or reconcile manually. (libsql: abort removes the re-homed COPY; the retained bare DB is the rollback target — see docs/default-scope-migration.md.) |
| `-i, --interactive` | — | — | — | Interactive (question-driven) migration: show the plan, PROMPT at each decision point (a name collision → rename / skip / abort), then stage honoring your answers. The guided CLI flow over the same `plan` + apply engine the console wizard uses. OFFLINE (node stopped) |
| `--node-config <NODE_CONFIG>` | — | `boatramp.cfg` | — | Node config (`boatramp.cfg` shape) used by `--finalize` to locate the libsql dir (+ the blob retired marker) for the substrate-complete gate. Defaults to `boatramp.cfg` |

### `boatramp project export`

Export a project's data (managed DB dumps + the control-plane KV slice + blobs) to a portable BRPROJ bundle, streamed from the RUNNING node (`Project·Admin` on the project)

**Usage:** `boatramp project export [OPTIONS] <NAME>`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<NAME>` | — | — | — | The project to export |
| `--out <OUT>` | — | — | — | Write the bundle to this file (the streamed default). Mutually exclusive with `--resumable`; exactly one is required |
| `--resumable <DIR_NAME>` | — | — | — | RESUMABLE export: write a member-object directory of this NAME on the NODE (under the node's configured `[serve] resumable_export_dir` base) instead of streaming a file — an interrupted run RESUMES instead of restarting. The directory is node-local (that is what lets it resume); the name is relative and host-confined |
| `--mode <MODE>` | — | — | differential \| incremental | DELTA export: `differential` (vs a fixed base) or `incremental` (vs the parent, forming a chain). Only with `--resumable`; requires `--base`. Ships only what changed since the base (KV + blob true-deltas today; SQL falls back to a full dump within the delta bundle). Default: a full (non-delta) export |
| `--base <DIR_NAME>` | — | — | — | The base (differential) / parent (incremental) resumable-dir NAME to chain the delta onto (a prior `--resumable` export on the same node). Required with `--mode` |
| `--full` | — | — | — | Export a FULL bundle (schema + data). Default: `--data-only` (app data only — no identity/RBAC/routing) |
| `--include-identity` | — | — | — | Include the identity transport container (the project KEK, passphrase-wrapped) for a same-environment RECOVERY. Implies a FULL bundle; requires a transport key (--transport-key-file, else BOATRAMP_EXPORT_TRANSPORT_KEY, else an interactive prompt). Local KEK envelopes only |
| `--transport-key-file <FILE>` | — | — | — | File holding the transport passphrase that wraps/opens the identity container |

### `boatramp project import`

Import a BRPROJ bundle into a project on the RUNNING node (`Project·Admin` on the target). Dry-run (a plan, no mutation) unless `--apply`

**Usage:** `boatramp project import [OPTIONS] <NAME>`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<NAME>` | — | — | — | The project to import into |
| `--in <FILE>` | — | — | — | The bundle file to import (the streamed default). Mutually exclusive with `--resumable`; exactly one is required |
| `--resumable <DIR_NAME>` | — | — | — | RESUMABLE import: read a member-object directory of this NAME on the NODE (under the node's configured `[serve] resumable_export_dir` base — the output of a resumable export) instead of sending a file. Host-confined relative name |
| `--clone-from <SOURCE_URL>` | — | — | — | STREAMING CLONE: pull the project from a LIVE source node over the network instead of a bundle file — the target fetches the source manifest, diffs its own store, and restores only the missing members (no bundle lands anywhere). This is the source node's base URL. `Project·Admin` on BOTH nodes (not node-global). Mutually exclusive with `--in`/`--resumable` |
| `--clone-source-project <PROJECT>` | — | — | — | The SOURCE project to clone (only with `--clone-from`). Defaults to the target project NAME — the common same-name env-clone |
| `--clone-source-token-file <FILE>` | — | — | — | File holding the operator's SOURCE-node Project-Admin token for `--clone-from` (falls back to BOATRAMP_CLONE_SOURCE_TOKEN). The token is sent in a header over TLS, never on the command line |
| `--clone-data-only` | — | — | — | Pull a `--data-only` clone (app data only — no control-plane KV). Only with `--clone-from` |
| `--clone-verify` | — | — | — | Stream-level VERIFY a clone (only with `--clone-from`, no `--apply`): open the source stream and validate the whole bundle end-to-end WITHOUT mutating the target. The default `--clone-from` dry-run is instead the CHEAP PLAN (manifest + diff only — no stream); use this when you want the heavier, full end-to-end validation a plan does not perform |
| `--apply` | — | — | — | Execute the import (default: a dry-run plan — mutate nothing) |
| `--force` | — | — | — | Overlay a non-empty control-plane KV destination (the commingle override; only meaningful for a FULL bundle) |
| `--allow-schema-skew` | — | — | — | Proceed despite a Postgres schema-ledger fingerprint mismatch between the bundle and the target |
| `--overwrite` | — | — | — | Replace an EXISTING target project (one that already holds its own KV/blob data). Default off — a clone into a fresh target is the safe default; this is opt-in |
| `--identity <IDENTITY>` | — | `fresh` | fresh \| adopt | Identity decision: `fresh` (default — the target mints its own identity and source-sealed secrets are dropped) or `adopt` (install the bundle's KEK for a same-environment recovery; requires a transport key) |
| `--transport-key-file <FILE>` | — | — | — | File holding the transport passphrase (for `--identity adopt`). Falls back to BOATRAMP_EXPORT_TRANSPORT_KEY, then an interactive prompt |
| `--enumerate-mismatches` | — | — | — | Clone robustness — ASSESS SCOPE: scan every member and report EVERY declared≠streamed integrity mismatch (path + class: der/base/primary) in one pass, then FAIL at the end, instead of aborting at the first. Applies nothing that mismatches — an assessment, so pair it with a dry-run (no `--apply`) or `--clone-verify`. Tells you "1 stale blob or many?" before any fix-blind retry |
| `--skip-member-mismatch` | — | — | — | Clone robustness — GET THE CLONE THROUGH: WARN + CONTINUE past a member whose stored bytes disagree with its declared size/checksum, instead of hard-failing. DEFAULT-scoped to re-generable `der/` image derivatives (the target re-derives a skipped one on access); a mismatch on a baseline, a primary/original blob, or any DB/KV/identity member STILL hard-fails. Broaden with `--skip-member-mismatch-any-blob` |
| `--skip-member-mismatch-any-blob` | — | — | — | Clone robustness — the LOUDER opt-in: broaden `--skip-member-mismatch` beyond `der/` derivatives to ANY blob member (baselines + primaries too). NEVER tolerates a non-blob (DB/KV/identity) member even so. Dangerous — it blesses a truncation on load-bearing blob data; prefer fixing the source (`blob reconcile`/`blob purge`). Requires `--skip-member-mismatch` |
| `--continue-on-error <KINDS>` | — | — | — | Clone robustness — GET THE TRANSFER THROUGH past a per-blob FAILURE (not just an integrity mismatch): forgive the listed error kinds (warn, record, skip that one blob, then continue) instead of aborting the whole op. Bare `--continue-on-error` forgives EVERY kind; `--continue-on-error=backend,member-mismatch` forgives only those. The kinds are `backend` (a blob target-write that survived the backend's retries and the complete HEAD-recovery) and `member-mismatch` (the integrity mismatch — the generalised home of `--skip-member-mismatch`). Each skipped blob lands in a skip MANIFEST the op reports, for `--only-blobs` repair. Default off (hard-fail the first failure) |
| `--only-blobs <MANIFEST>` | — | — | — | Clone robustness — REPAIR: re-stream ONLY the blob keys named in this skip MANIFEST (the file a prior `--continue-on-error` run wrote), restoring nothing else. The blobs are pulled again from the source over the SAME streaming path (no local copy, no spool). The manifest is the JSON the op reported; read locally and its keys forwarded to the node |

## `boatramp dns`

Configure DNS + issue wildcard preview certs (requires `--features acme-dns`)

**Usage:** `boatramp dns <COMMAND>`

### `boatramp dns setup`

Create the `*.deploy.<host>` record so by-id preview subdomains resolve to this server

**Usage:** `boatramp dns setup [OPTIONS]`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--provider <PROVIDER>` | — | — | manual \| cloudflare \| route53 \| oci \| digitalocean \| hetzner \| ns1 \| dnsimple \| gcp-dns \| azure-dns \| akamai | DNS provider (`manual` prints the record to create by hand) |
| `--host <HOST>` | — | — | — | The site host, e.g. `example.com` (the record is `*.deploy.<host>`) |
| `--target <TARGET>` | — | — | — | Where the wildcard points: an IPv4/IPv6 address (→ A/AAAA) or another hostname (→ CNAME) |
| `--ttl <TTL>` | — | `120` | — | Record TTL (seconds) |

### `boatramp dns configure-domain`

Point a **verified** custom domain (apex or sub-domain) at this server by upserting its A/AAAA/CNAME record via the provider. Verify ownership first (`boatramp domain add/verify`) — never point a host you don't control

**Usage:** `boatramp dns configure-domain [OPTIONS] <HOST>`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<HOST>` | — | — | — | The custom hostname, e.g. `www.example.com` or the apex `example.com` |
| `--provider <PROVIDER>` | — | — | manual \| cloudflare \| route53 \| oci \| digitalocean \| hetzner \| ns1 \| dnsimple \| gcp-dns \| azure-dns \| akamai | DNS provider (`manual` prints the record to create by hand) |
| `--target <TARGET>` | — | — | — | Where it points: an IPv4/IPv6 address (→ A/AAAA) or another hostname (→ CNAME; invalid at a true apex — use an address there) |
| `--ttl <TTL>` | — | `300` | — | Record TTL (seconds) |
| `--proxied` | — | — | — | Proxy the record through Cloudflare (orange-cloud: cache/WAF/edge TLS). Cloudflare-only; ignored by other providers, and forces automatic TTL |
| `--disable-cf-universal-ssl` | — | — | — | Cloudflare + wildcard host only: if the zone's **Universal SSL** is enabled, disable it. Its ACME domain-control-validation TXT at `_acme-challenge.<zone>` otherwise clobbers a wildcard's DNS-01 delegation (e.g. a fly wildcard cert), so the wildcard never issues. Safe on a **DNS-only** (not `--proxied`) zone whose edge cert is unused; needs a token with `Zone.SSL and Certificates:Edit`. Without this flag, a clear warning is printed instead |

### `boatramp dns cert`

Issue (or renew) the `*.deploy.<host>` wildcard certificate via ACME DNS-01, into the cert cache `boatramp serve --tls acme-dns` reads

**Usage:** `boatramp dns cert [OPTIONS]`

| Argument | Env | Default | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--provider <PROVIDER>` | — | — | manual \| cloudflare \| route53 \| oci \| digitalocean \| hetzner \| ns1 \| dnsimple \| gcp-dns \| azure-dns \| akamai | — |
| `--host <HOST>` | — | — | — | The site host; the cert covers `*.deploy.<host>` |
| `--acme-directory <ACME_DIRECTORY>` | — | `https://acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory` | — | ACME directory URL (defaults to Let's Encrypt production) |
| `--acme-contact <ACME_CONTACT>` | — | — | — | Contact email for the ACME account |
| `--cache <CACHE>` | — | `./data/acme` | — | Certificate cache directory |
